prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1012; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a side impact at an intersection involving the insured's vehicle, with the claimant reporting whiplash. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Verified that the driver involved is named on the policy and that the coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the policy records suggests any issue with the timing of coverage.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and matches the general description of the collision given to us.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photos submitted by the insured. They confirm the point of impact and several of the reported details, though no independent witnesses have come forward to add to the account.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage appears largely consistent with the side impact as described. The estimator's notes are attached to the file for reference.

Entry 6: A few older scratches were noted on the vehicle. They may predate this collision, and I have asked the appraiser to separate them from the new damage in the estimate.

Entry 7: Claimant's attorney submitted the initial medical summary, which describes whiplash symptoms. The kind and force of the reported injury line up reasonably well with the crash as described.

Entry 8: Reviewed the claimant's prior medical history provided through the attorney. No earlier injury to the same body area is on record.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury. I have requested the treatment notes to understand the course of care.

Entry 10: Claimant later supplied a few additional details about the collision through counsel. The core account has not changed from the original statement.

Entry 11: Reviewed the damage estimate against the photos and the described impact. Most of the repair items fit the collision, and the remaining items are being checked against the older scratches noted earlier.

Entry 12: File is pending review of the treatment records and the final repair estimate. No further action is needed until the medical and repair documentation is complete.
